title: The Resurrection of Jesus
subtitle: Every place that points to it, from Isaac on the mountain and Jonah in the fish to the empty tomb, the people who saw him, and what it means for us
summary: "Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures, He was buried, He was raised on the third day according to the Scriptures" (1 Corinthians 15:3–4). Paul calls this the message "of first importance," and he says the Scriptures pointed to it. On the road to Emmaus Jesus himself, "beginning with Moses and all the Prophets," explained what was written about him. This study follows that thread: pictures in Israel's stories (Isaac received back, Joseph alive, Jonah given back by the sea, the third day again and again), hope in the Psalms and Prophets that God would not leave his Holy One in the grave, the people raised before Easter who all died again, Jesus's own predictions, the empty tomb, the people who saw him, the apostles' preaching, and what his rising means for everyone who belongs to him. Each Old Testament passage is marked by how plainly it points ahead: some the New Testament quotes outright, some the early church read this way, and some are patterns many readers see. Start on the map: click a branch to zoom into it, and a dot to see where it leads.

groups.title: Pictures and patterns
groups.note: Stories in which someone is as good as dead and given back, often on the third day. Hebrews reads Isaac this way outright; others are patterns the church has long seen.

refs.label: Isaac on the mountain
refs.note: “On the third day” Abraham sees the place, and tells his servants “we will return to you.” A ram is offered in Isaac's place.

links.topic: “He did receive Isaac back from death”

refs.note: Joseph holds his brothers three days, then offers them life.

refs.note: Thrown into Elisha's tomb, he “was revived and stood up on his feet.”

groups.title: The empty tomb
groups.note: A sealed and guarded tomb, found open and empty on the first day of the week, first by women, then by Peter and John.

refs.label: The guard and the seal
refs.note: His enemies remembered what his friends forgot: “After three days I will rise again.”

refs.label: “He is not here; He has risen, just as He said!”
refs.note: An earthquake, an angel who rolls away the stone and sits on it, and guards who become like dead men.

refs.label: “Who will roll away the stone?”
refs.note: Three women come with spices at sunrise and find the stone already rolled back.

refs.label: “Why do you look for the living among the dead?”
refs.note: The women are told to remember his words; the apostles think it nonsense; Peter runs to see the linen cloths.

refs.label: The linen cloths lying there
refs.note: Peter and the other disciple run to the tomb; the head cloth is rolled up by itself. “He saw and believed. For they still did not understand from the Scripture that Jesus had to rise from the dead.”

links.label: Psalm 16:10
links.topic: The Scripture they had not yet understood

refs.label: “His disciples came by night and stole Him away”
refs.note: The guards are paid to tell it, which admits that the tomb was empty.

groups.title: He appeared
groups.note: Not a vision in the dark: he was seen by women and men, alone and in groups, indoors and outdoors, eating, touched, over forty days.

refs.label: “They came to Him, grasped His feet, and worshiped Him”
Mary Magdalene: “I have seen the Lord!”
refs.note: She thinks he is the gardener until he says her name.

refs.label: The road to Emmaus
refs.note: “Beginning with Moses and all the Prophets, He explained to them what was written in all the Scriptures about Himself,” and they knew him when he broke the bread. Back in Jerusalem: “The Lord has indeed risen and has appeared to Simon!”

refs.label: “Touch Me and see”
refs.note: “A spirit does not have flesh and bones, as you see I have.” He eats fish in front of them, then opens their minds: “The Christ will suffer and rise from the dead on the third day.”

refs.label: Through locked doors: “Peace be with you!”
refs.note: He shows them his hands and his side.

refs.label: Thomas: “My Lord and my God!”
refs.note: “Put your finger here and look at My hands.”

refs.label: Breakfast on the shore
refs.note: “This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.”

refs.label: On the mountain in Galilee
refs.note: “They worshiped Him, but some doubted.” Then the Great Commission.

refs.label: “Many convincing proofs that He was alive”
refs.note: Over forty days, speaking about the kingdom of God.

refs.label: Cephas, the Twelve, five hundred, James, and last of all Paul
refs.note: Written about twenty years after, while “most of whom are still living” could be asked.

refs.label: Stephen: “I see heaven open”
refs.note: “And the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God.”

refs.label: Paul on the Damascus road
refs.note: “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.”

refs.label: “I was dead, and behold, now I am alive forever and ever!”
refs.note: To John on Patmos: “I hold the keys of Death and of Hades.”

groups.title: The apostles preached it
groups.note: From the first sermon on, the resurrection is the center of the message, argued from the Scriptures and from eyewitnesses.

refs.label: Peter at Pentecost
refs.note: “God raised Him from the dead, releasing Him from the agony of death, because it was impossible for death to keep Him in its grip.”

refs.label: “You killed the Author of life, but God raised Him”
refs.note: “And we are witnesses of this fact.”

refs.label: The rejected stone, raised
refs.note: Peter before the council: healed “by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom you crucified but whom God raised from the dead.”

refs.label: “Their testimony about the resurrection of the Lord Jesus”
“Who ate and drank with Him after He rose”
refs.note: “God raised Him up on the third day and caused Him to be seen.”

refs.label: Paul at Pisidian Antioch
refs.note: The resurrection proclaimed from Psalm 2, Isaiah 55 and Psalm 16.

refs.label: In Athens: “Jesus and the resurrection”
refs.note: God “has given proof of this to everyone by raising Him from the dead.” Some mocked; others wanted to hear more.

refs.label: “Why would any of you consider it incredible that God raises the dead?”
refs.note: Before King Agrippa: nothing “beyond what the prophets and Moses said would happen.”

links.label: Luke 24:44–47
links.topic: What is written in the Law, the Prophets and the Psalms

groups.title: What it means, now and at the end
groups.note: His rising declares who he is, puts us right with God, gives us new life now, and promises bodies raised like his.

refs.label: Declared the Son of God with power
refs.note: “By His resurrection from the dead.”

refs.label: “Raised to life for our justification”
Newness of life
refs.note: Buried with him in baptism, raised to walk in newness of life. “Christ … cannot die again; death no longer has dominion over Him.”

links.label: Colossians 2:12
links.topic: Buried with him, raised with him

refs.label: The Spirit will give life to your mortal bodies

links.label: Ezekiel 37:14
links.topic: “I will put My Spirit in you and you will live”

refs.label: “Believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead”
refs.note: “And you will be saved.”

refs.label: “If Christ has not been raised”
refs.note: “Our preaching is worthless, and so is your faith … you are still in your sins.” But “Christ has indeed been raised.”

refs.label: Sown perishable, raised imperishable
refs.note: Like a seed and the plant that grows from it: “It is sown a natural body; it is raised a spiritual body.”

refs.label: “We will all be changed”
refs.note: “In the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet … Death has been swallowed up in victory.”

refs.label: “Will also raise us with Jesus”

links.label: 1 Thessalonians 4:14
links.topic: “God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep”

refs.label: The power that raised him, at work in us
refs.note: “Which He exerted in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand.”

refs.label: “The power of His resurrection”
refs.note: He “will transform our lowly bodies to be like His glorious body.”

refs.label: “Since you have been raised with Christ”
refs.note: “Strive for the things above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.”

refs.label: “The dead in Christ will be the first to rise”
refs.note: “So that you will not grieve like the rest, who are without hope.”

refs.label: “He always lives to intercede for them”
refs.note: Priests died and were replaced; “because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.”

refs.label: “A living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ”
“The dead will hear the voice of the Son of God”
refs.note: “All who are in their graves will hear His voice and come out.”

refs.label: “I will raise him up at the last day”
“There will be no more death”
refs.note: “Behold, I make all things new.”

links.label: Isaiah 25:8
links.topic: “He will swallow up death forever”
